identity.real_world_identity_notes: Porsche 911 GT3 Cup built by Porsche Motorsport for its one-make Carrera Cup and Supercup championships, running a 3,996 cc flat six of 485 hp through a six-speed dog-type gearbox shifted by paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies neither, and the clutch is needed to pull away.

The gearbox is dog-type, which is stated by the registered source rather than inferred. A dog box would ordinarily want a rev-matched downshift, but this car blips its own, so the driver is not asked for one.
The registered source adds a triple-disc sintered metal racing clutch and pneumatic gearshift activation.
The two Cup cars share a gearbox specification and were driven separately; nothing is inherited between them.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.porsche-911-gt3-cup-4-0.20260817t053533610z-cdfa71d6 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is stated by a registered source.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the car, its engine and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source states a six-speed dog-type gearbox operated by paddles, and the live drive selected six paddle gears with automatic cut and blip and a clutch needed to pull away.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Porsche dog-type gearbox, but the car blips its own downshifts, so there is no rev-matching to do. The clutch is needed only to pull away.
